statement: Given values representing the heights of consecutive unit-width bars arranged circularly, determine the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle that can be formed entirely underneath the bars. The bars are considered adjacent in a circle so an interval may wrap from the end of values around to the beginning. The rectangle must span one or more consecutive bars in this circular order and its height is limited by the minimum height among the bars it covers.

    # stack holds indices with increasing heights
    stack = []
    # iterate with sentinel 0 height at end to flush
    for i in range(n+1):

        while stack and cur_h < values[stack[-1]]:
            h = values[stack.pop()]

        stack.append(i)

solver_source:
def solve(params):
    values = params["values"]
    n = len(values)
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    # standard non-wrapping max via monotonic stack
    best = 0
    stack = []
    for i in range(n+1):
        cur = values[i] if i < n else 0
        while stack and cur < values[stack[-1]]:
            h = values[stack.pop()]
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
            width = i - left - 1
            area = h * width
            if area > best:
                best = area
        stack.append(i)
    # wrapping intervals must contain both first and last element (cross the seam)
    # any wrapping interval is determined by a left suffix [l..n-1] and right prefix [0..r]
    # with l>0, total length = (n-l)+r+1, height = min(min_suffix[l], min_prefix[r])
    # precompute suffix minima and prefix minima
    pref_min = [0]*n
    cur = values[0]
    pref_min[0]=cur
    for i in range(1,n):
        if values[i] < cur:
            cur = values[i]
        pref_min[i]=cur
    suff_min = [0]*n
    cur = values[n-1]
    suff_min[n-1]=cur
    for i in range(n-2,-1,-1):
        if values[i] < cur:
            cur = values[i]
        suff_min[i]=cur
    # enumerate all wrapping intervals via l and r
    # O(n^2) worst but with O(1) height lookup
    for l in range(1, n):
        hs = suff_min[l]
        for r in range(n):
            # avoid double counting non-wrapping and full circle beyond n
            length = (n - l) + (r + 1)
            if length > n or length <= 0:
                continue
            # if interval does not actually wrap (needs both sides) skip if already counted
            # wrapping requires l <= n-1 and includes seam, which it does by construction
            h = hs if hs < pref_min[r] else pref_min[r]
            area = h * length
            if area > best:
                best = area
            # early break if height becomes too small to beat best with max possible remaining length
            # (optional pruning)
    return int(best)
